title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook
author: Daniel Cheng
content:
Summary:
This playbook documents Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response process: severity taxonomy, escalation paths, runbook templates, postmortem requirements, rotation policies, game day guidance, and status page / customer communication templates. It is intended for SREs, on-call engineers, product owners, and support staff.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to all production incidents that affect Redwood hosted, Dedicated, or Private customer-facing inference services.
- Focuses on minimizing customer impact, restoring service, preserving evidence for RCA, and communicating clearly to stakeholders.
- Does NOT replace component-level runbooks; those live under eng-platform and eng-serving-runtime runbook pages.

1) Incident severity and SLO thresholds:
- Sev-1 (P0): Full production outage / API unavailable or >90% error rate for >5 minutes, customer-facing data loss, or security incident with active impact. Response target: acknowledge in 1 minute, primary on-call involvement within 5 minutes.
- Sev-2 (P1): Significant degradation (high latency, partial feature outage) impacting many customers or a single enterprise customer with SLA. Response target: acknowledge in 5 minutes, mitigation plan within 30 minutes.
- Sev-3 (P2): Low-impact degradation, non-urgent customer reports, or single-user issues. Response target: acknowledge in 1 business hour, resolution or workaround planned within 72 hours.

SLO/alert thresholds (examples):
- API 99th percentile latency > 2x baseline for 10 minutes => Sev-2 alert.
- 5xx error rate > 5% across 5 minutes or >10% for 1 minute => Sev-1 alert.
- KV cache miss spike leading to >30% token cost increase over baseline for 30 minutes => Sev-2.

2) Roles & responsibilities:
- Primary On-call (Owner): First responder; owns triage, mitigation, and handoff.
- Secondary On-call (Backup): Available to assist/replace primary if escalation or fatigue.
- Incident Commander (IC): For Sev-1/2 incidents, coordinates across teams, external comms, and postmortem ownership. Typically a senior SRE or engineering manager.
- Communications Lead: Writes status page and customer-facing messages, works with legal/security for restricted incidents.
- Product/PO Representative: Assesses customer impact and prioritizes business responses.
- Postmortem Author: Documents timeline and RCA within 72 hours for Sev-1/2.

3) Triage & escalation procedure (high-level):
1. Alert fires in PagerDuty / Opsgenie -> Primary on-call receives notification.
2. Primary acknowledges the alert within the severity target window.
3. Primary performs quick triage (check dashboards, runbook, recent deploys) and sets severity.
4. If Sev-1 or if unclear: escalate immediately to Secondary and notify IC.
5. IC declares incident and creates the incident channel (Slack #incident-<id>) and incident doc (Confluence incident page).
6. Start a staggered rotation for 15-minute status updates until stabilized; then move to 1-hour cadence.
7. When mitigated, IC declares the incident mitigated, documents timeline, and schedules postmortem.

4) Runbook structure & templates (must exist for every major service):
- Title, scope, owner, last updated date, contact list (pager, slack, email), severity mapping.
- Pre-incident checks: dashboards, recent deploys, infra alerts, capacity metrics.
- Step-by-step mitigation instructions (ordered, with commands and expected outputs).
- Workaround and rollback procedures.
- Post-incident validation and follow-up tasks.

Runbook example: API gateway 5xx surge (short):
1. Check API gateway error rate: kubectl -n platform get deployment api-gateway && curl -s https://metrics.internal/api/errors
2. Identify upstream service causing 5xx via logs (k8s fluentd / Loki): query = {component="api"} | json | status >= 500
3. If a specific upstream is failing, scale replicas: kubectl scale deploy <service> --replicas=3 and monitor error rate for 5 minutes.
4. If traffic spike from a customer: apply request-rate limit rule for their API key in the gateway for 15 minutes.
5. If recent deploy suspected: rollback to previous revision and monitor.

5) Postmortem & RCA requirements:
- Required for all Sev-1 and Sev-2 incidents. Postmortem must be created within 72 hours and include:
  - Title, incident ID, severity, owners, timeline (with timestamps), root cause, contributing factors, mitigations taken, customer impact, detection method, and action items with owners and due dates.
  - A blameless language section and lessons learned.
  - Link to relevant logs, traces, runbooks, commits, and deploy IDs.
- Action items tracked in a visible backlog (label: incident-action) and reviewed in next oncall retro.

6) On-call rotations and handoffs:
- Primary rotation: 1-week shifts by default for SRE team; engineering teams with low headcount may use 1-week or 2-week with backup.
- Shift start: Monday 09:00 PT. Handoff checklist: outstanding incidents, paging status, ongoing mitigations, outstanding action items, and list of contacts.
- Handoff process: create Handoff note in Slack #oncall-handoffs and update the rotation calendar.
- Escalation path: Primary -> Secondary (15 minutes) -> IC/Manager (30 minutes) -> PagerDuty escalation policy continues to follow contact list.

7) Game days and readiness drills:
- Quarterly game days run by eng-sre to validate runbooks, telemetry, and on-call readiness.
- Game day structure: objective, scope, inject timeline, expected outcomes, and post-game retrospective.
- Required participants: Primary on-call, secondary, 1 service owner, 1 infra owner, and a communications lead.
- Deliverables: updated runbooks, identified blind spots, and assigned remediation actions.

8) Status page & customer communications templates:
Customer-facing status page principles:
- Must be timely, factual, and clear. Avoid technical jargon. Confirmed updates only.
- For Sev-1 incidents provide updates every 30–60 minutes until mitigated.

Example status page timeline (short):
- 2026-03-04 09:12 UTC — Investigating: We are aware of degraded API responses affecting inference requests. Engineers are investigating. (Initial notification)
- 2026-03-04 09:45 UTC — Identified: We have identified a problem with the API gateway affecting ~30% of requests. Mitigation in progress.
- 2026-03-04 10:05 UTC — Mitigated: Traffic throttling and replica scaling reduced errors to <1%. Full remediation in progress.
- 2026-03-04 11:30 UTC — Resolved: Root cause was a faulty deploy. A rollback completed and monitoring shows healthy metrics. Postmortem scheduled.

Customer communication templates (short):
- Initial customer-facing message:
  Subject: Incident affecting Redwood Inference API — [INV-2026-XXXX]
  Body: We are investigating reports of degraded API responses impacting inference requests. Our engineering team is actively investigating and we will provide updates within 30 minutes. No action is required from customers at this time.

- Follow-up update (identified):
  Subject: Update on incident INV-2026-XXXX — mitigation in progress
  Body: We identified the root cause and applied a mitigation that has reduced errors. We continue to monitor and will provide the next update in 30–60 minutes.

- Post-incident customer summary:
  Subject: Incident INV-2026-XXXX — summary & impact
  Body: On 2026-03-04 at 09:12 UTC we experienced degraded API responses due to a failed deploy to the API gateway which produced elevated 5xx responses. Impact: ~30% of requests for 45 minutes. Mitigation: rollback and replica scaling; no data loss. Next steps: postmortem and remedial actions scheduled; customers will be notified when fixes are implemented.

9) Communication channels & tooling:
- PagerDuty (primary paging), Opsgenie (backup), Slack incident channels (#incident-<id>), status.redwood.ai for public status, and Confluence for incident docs.
- Dashboards: per-route latency, per-model token cost, 5xx/error budget, queue lengths, GPU utilization. All runbooks must include direct links to the dashboards they rely on.

10) Post-incident review and retrospective:
- Within 7 days schedule a blameless postmortem review with SRE, service owners, and product reps.
- Track action items with owners, target dates, and closure criteria.
- Use the postmortem to update runbooks, alerts, and SLO thresholds where appropriate.

11) Runbook maintenance & ownership:
- Every runbook must have a designated owner and a last-updated date. Owners review runbooks quarterly or after any relevant incident.
- Minor edits can be made ad hoc; substantive changes require reviewer sign-off and a short changelog entry on the runbook page.

Appendix: quick checklists
- Initial triage checklist (first 10 minutes): acknowledge alert, identify scope, check recent deploys, create incident channel and Confluence page, escalate per severity.
- Mitigation checklist (first 30 minutes): apply short-term mitigations, stabilize traffic, enable throttles/limits if needed, communicate externally.
- Post-incident checklist (first 72 hours): create postmortem draft, capture timeline, assign action items, schedule review.

Contacts and escalation matrix:
- Eng-SRE PagerDuty: primary -> secondary -> IC; PagerDuty escalation details live in eng-sre/pagerduty-config.
- On-call Slack channel: #oncall-alerts (ops notifications) and #incident-<id> for active incidents.

Document maintenance:
- Owner: Eng-SRE (Daniel Cheng)
- Review cadence: Annual + after every Sev-1 incident or serious Sev-2.
- Last reviewed: 2026-03-04

Related pages & templates:
- Refer to eng-platform runbooks, SLO and error budget pages, and the Confluence incident postmortem template.

End of playbook.
